name: bandit captain
desc:
It takes a strong personality, ruthless cunning, and a silver tongue to keep a gang of bandits in line. The **bandit captain** has these qualities in spades.

In addition to managing a crew of selfish malcontents, the **pirate captain** is a variation of the bandit captain, with a ship to protect and command. To keep the crew in line, the captain must mete out rewards and punishment on a regular basis.

More than treasure, a bandit captain or pirate captain craves infamy. A prisoner who appeals to the captain’s vanity or ego is more likely to be treated fairly than a prisoner who does not or claims not to know anything of the captain’s colorful reputation.

actions.name: multiattack
actions.desc: The captain makes three melee attacks: two with its scimitar and one with its dagger. Or the captain makes two ranged attacks with its daggers.

actions.name: scimitar
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.

actions.name: dagger
actions.desc: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.

reactions.name: parry
reactions.desc: The captain adds 2 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the captain must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

lore:
The Bandit Captain is a creature of the borders, found wherever the law’s reach falters. Unlike the common cutthroat, the Captain is a social apex predator, haunting ruined watchtowers and choked mountain passes. They do not merely steal; they harvest.

Their predatory behavior is marked by a cruel patience. They orchestrate ambushes not with mindless violence, but with the precision of a shepherd herding sheep into a slaughter-pen. A Captain commands through a synthesis of charisma and terror, turning a rabble into a singular, lethal organism. They study their prey from the treeline, identifying the weakest link long before a single blade is drawn.

In local folklore, they are often depicted as "The Shadowed King" or "The Toll-Gatherer of Graves." Peasants whisper that a Captain is born when a soldier loses his soul but keeps his sword. To encounter one is to face the dark reflection of civilization—a leader who has traded the crown for the noose, ruling over a kingdom of mud and blood. Beware the glint of polished steel in the brush; it is the eye of the wolf watching the fold.
